svg.text: one comparator per tap per sample, no multiplier

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: What sets the step size

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • large step: fast acquisition, noisy taps

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • small step: stable taps, slow to adapt

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • real links gear-shift: coarse then fine

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Adaptation is a control loop, not a filter

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Every equaliser in the chain has coefficients, and every coefficient has to be set. Some are set once at bring-up from a training

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: exchange; some adapt continuously from the slicer's own error. The loop that does the adapting is almost always a sign-sign LMS,

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: because at 50 gigabaud a multiplier per tap per sample is not affordable and a comparator is.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The error signal is the whole design. Before the link is trained there are no reliable decisions, so adaptation runs on a known

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pattern; after training it runs on the slicer's own output, which means a wrong decision corrupts the adaptation for a moment. That

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: is why adaptation bandwidth is a stability parameter, not a speed parameter.
